findings.message: The new info tooltip fails WCAG 1.4.13 (content on hover or focus). (1) Escape does not close it: there is no key handler, and CSS :focus-within keeps it open while the button has focus. (2) The pointer cannot reach it: the tooltip sits 8px below the button (`top:calc(100% + 8px)`), and the gap is outside `.dv-info`, so `:hover` drops as the pointer crosses it. (3) The page's lede now exists only inside this tooltip, and tapping a button does not focus it in iOS Safari, so touch users cannot read it. Fix: make the tooltip a disclosure (aria-expanded, toggled by click) that Escape closes, or bridge the gap with padding inside `.dv-info`. Keep the lede visible, or reachable without hover.
findings.scenario: Keyboard user tabs to the (i) on the Proposals page and presses Escape → the tooltip stays over the content. Mouse user moves from the icon toward the tooltip → it disappears before the pointer reaches it.

findings.message: When a session crosses midnight, the first day gets `commits: 0`. sync-time sends that as `CommitTime.commits = 0`. Time tests `c.commits ?`, `fromRepo` and `gitRef` for truthiness, so 0 reads as 'a webhook Time: line'. The suggestion is then worded as a single commit, gets `source_ref` `git:<KEY>/<day>`, agent "Git", and drops `commits`. Also, `Draft.commits` is `.positive()`, so 0 would fail its schema anyway. Fix: carry an explicit marker such as `source: "repo"`, or count the session's commits on every day it touches. Test the time handler with commits 0.
findings.scenario: Commits at 23:30 and 00:45 UTC → the day-1 estimate is {hours:1, commits:0} → the suggestion reads "Your commit FLT-101/ for FLT-101 says 1 h" and logs with source_ref `git:FLT-101/2026-11-12`, agent Git.

findings.message: `commits[].email`, `id` and `at` come from the pusher's payload, and the server cannot check them. Anyone with `delivery:proposal:push` on the project can make up commits under a colleague's verified email. That drafts suggestions in the colleague's name and writes audit and history lines naming them. Worse, the once-per-day claim in `commit_day_draft` then blocks that person's real hours for the day. The docs promise attribution 'never whoever pushed', but the pusher controls the email. Fix: only accept commits that can be verified (for example, attribute only when the pusher is the author, or check the commits against the provider), or at least record the pusher on the draft and don't let an unverified draft take the day.
findings.scenario: Engineer A pushes FLT-101 with commits [{email: B's verified email, at: 2026-11-12T09:00Z}] → B gets a 0.5 h suggestion and the history says "Drafted 0.5 h…". B's real commits for 12 Nov never draft, because the day is taken.

findings.message: Commits the webhook already drafted are left out only when the webhook ran first. `draftCommitTime` (commit-time.ts) never checks `commit_day_draft` or `repo:` entries, so when the sync runs first and the webhook later, the same commit drafts twice. The two drafts have different source_refs (`repo:` vs `git:`), so `alreadyLogged` does not catch it. Fix: make the dedupe go both ways. For example, the webhook skips a commit whose day/proposal is already in commit_day_draft, or the day draft records its commit ids in commit_draft.
findings.scenario: A dev runs /amax:sync-specclaw on 13 Nov before `git push`. A 12 Nov commit carrying `Time: 1.5h` is counted in the 1.75 h day estimate. The push webhook then drafts 1.5 h for the same commit → both are accepted → 3.25 h.

findings.message: The estimate splits hours into days by UTC date, and "days that have ended" uses the server's UTC date. Time places entries, weekends and weeks on the person's local day (`localToday`, entity zone). The two day rules disagree for any zone away from UTC, so drafts land on the wrong timesheet day and get the wrong weekend flag. Fix: split days by the author's local zone, using Time's rule through a contract.
findings.scenario: An Australian dev (UTC+10) commits 08:00–09:30 AEST on Mon 16 Nov → UTC Sun 15 Nov → the draft lands on Sunday, marked weekend, in the previous ISO week.

findings.message: Hours are drafted only for records that pass `refusal`. When the repo archives a change before a Prod deployment releases it, the push skips it as `released` (and on a branch as `back`/`stale`), so the commits of its final days are not drafted. Drafting waits until Prod catches up, possibly beyond `backdateWeeks`. Drafting time does not depend on whether the phase write is accepted. Fix: collect `timed` for any record matched to a stored, non-withdrawn proposal, including skipped ones.
findings.scenario: FLT-101 gets commits on 12 Nov and is archived the same day. The sync on 13 Nov sends phase released while the stored phase is verified → skipped 'released' → drafted: 0. Prod releases it 3 weeks later, and the person's back-date limit refuses the accept.

findings.message: The draft's hours are stored and audited (`commit_day_draft`, `delivery.commit_time.draft` after) without the read they came from: no `ref@sha`, no commit ids. Because the row is once per day, later corrections can't be traced to the push that produced the figure. Fix: store the source (`<ref>@<sha>`) and the commit ids in the row and in the audit after.
findings.scenario: The plugin on a branch and CI on main both carry 12 Nov commits. Whichever runs first wins with 1.75 h, and nothing records which push or which commits decided it.

findings.message: The list of waiting weeks takes the 8 newest weeks with any submitted timesheet across the tenant, and only then filters by `canApprove`. An approver's own pending weeks fall out when 8 newer weeks are waiting on other approvers. Fix: filter on the weeks this viewer can approve before applying the limit, or page until 8 approvable weeks are found.
findings.scenario: Maya (PM on CON) has a W40 week waiting. Other entities have submitted weeks in W41–W48 → the Overview shows Maya nothing to review.

findings.message: The draft line always reads "…waiting to be accepted", from an audit row written when the draft was made. After the person accepts or dismisses it, the history still says it is waiting. That is a false state, and next to the accepted 'logged' line it reads as double time. Fix: word it as an event ('Drafted 1.5 h for 12 Nov from the repo'), or resolve the line against the suggestion's current status.
findings.scenario: Kasun accepts the 12 Nov draft → the history shows both 'Kasun Dias logged 1.5 h' and 'Drafted 1.5 h … waiting to be accepted'. Or Kasun dismisses it → the history still says waiting.

findings.message: A failed `git log` returns [], the same as 'no commits named for the change'. Return undefined, or leave `commits` out, so the payload says the read was not made.

`consentOf` takes `since` from `commit_time.notified_at`. `setCommitTimeLogging` sets that column with `coalesce(excluded.notified_at, notified_at)`, so it stays at the first time commit time was switched on. When an Admin switches it off and later on again, the sync drafts hours from commits made while it was off. This also adds a second consent rule next to `commitTimeOn` (commit-time.ts:37), and the two can disagree. Fix: keep one consent rule in commit-time.ts that returns the start of the current enabled period. Store an `enabled_since` that is reset on every off→on switch, or keep the switch history, and have both the webhook and the sync use it.
findings.scenario: Entity switched on 2026-10-01, off 2026-10-20, on again 2026-11-10. A sync on 11-13 that carries commits from 10-25 drafts timesheet suggestions for 10-25, while consent was off.

findings.message: A push that only drafts hours returns outcome `unchanged`, writes no `sync_push` row, and the row has no drafted/unlinked columns. The Repo sync card never shows drafts.
"Waiting" counts entries in draft and rejected weeks too, but the card labels the total "waiting for approval", although nothing has been submitted.
The lede assertion and the 'Where time went' legend check were dropped instead of being replaced with the clock pinned or with checks on the current week, so the e2e no longer checks either.
The info button is inside <h1>, so the heading's accessible name becomes 'Proposals About proposals and how to add one'. Put the icon beside the h1, not inside it.

A squash- or rebase-merge writes new commits with new ids and, for a squash, a new author date. The squash subject usually names the change (this repo's own history: d4d2306a, b14aa8c1). The default-branch sync then counts that commit as fresh work and drafts at least 0.5 h on the merge day. `commit_day_draft`'s per-day key only catches this when the merge falls on a day already drafted. Fix: leave out commits whose subject or body has more than one `specclaw(<slug>)` line (squash bodies), or that also exist as a pre-squash commit already drafted. Cover merge, squash and rebase in the test.
findings.scenario: Branch commits on 11-10 are drafted from the branch sync. The PR is squash-merged on 11-12 with the subject 'specclaw(104-x): …'. The CI sync on main drafts an extra 0.5 h for 11-12 for the PR author.

findings.message: The 'day has ended' cutoff uses `new Date()`. Delivery's date windows use the tenant's `delivery.clock_pin` when there is one (README 'Today'), so this is a second 'today' rule that disagrees on pinned tenants. Use Delivery's today helper.
findings.scenario: On the e2e tenant, pinned to 2026-10-16, a sync drafts commits from 10-17 onward as 'ended' days.

findings.message: `waiting` counts every live entry in a week that isn't approved, draft weeks included. An entry in an unsubmitted week is labelled 'waiting for approval' though nobody has been asked to approve it. Count submitted weeks only, or label the figure 'not yet approved'.
findings.scenario: A repo draft is accepted into a draft week. The Time card shows '1.5 h waiting for approval' before the week is submitted.
